primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Bartter syndrome type IV due to BSND (barttin) deficiency
mechanism: Barttin, encoded by BSND, is an essential accessory beta subunit for ClC-Ka and ClC-Kb chloride channels in renal and inner-ear epithelia. Loss of barttin impairs basolateral chloride exit in the thick ascending limb and inner ear, causing severe renal salt wasting with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis and sensorineural deafness.
vignette: A newborn has polyhydramnios-associated prematurity, polyuria, poor weight gain, hypokalemia, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, elevated renin and aldosterone, and normal blood pressure. Newborn hearing testing shows bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in BSND.
lead: Which of the following transport abnormalities most directly explains the combination of renal salt wasting and hearing loss?
correct: Impaired function and membrane localization of ClC-K chloride channels in renal and inner-ear epithelia due to loss of their barttin accessory subunit
distractors: Loss of the apical Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb with normal inner-ear chloride-channel function
Loss of the apical ROMK potassium channel in the thick ascending limb with preserved cochlear ion transport
Loss of the basolateral ClC-Kb channel alone in the distal nephron without impairment of ClC-Ka
Loss of the thiazide-sensitive NaCl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule
distractor_notes: SLC12A1/NKCC2 loss causes Bartter type I but does not characteristically produce sensorineural deafness.
KCNJ1/ROMK loss causes Bartter type II but does not explain the inner-ear phenotype.
CLCNKB defects cause classic Bartter type III; barttin supports both ClC-Ka and ClC-Kb in kidney and inner ear.
SLC12A3 loss causes Gitelman syndrome, usually a later-onset distal convoluted-tubule salt-wasting disorder without congenital deafness.
key_expl: BSND encodes barttin, an accessory subunit required for normal ClC-Ka/ClC-Kb chloride-channel function in the kidney and inner ear. Severe loss of barttin produces Bartter type IV: renal salt wasting with secondary hyperreninemic hyperaldosteronism and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, together with sensorineural deafness.
objective: Explain Bartter type IV as loss of barttin-dependent ClC-K chloride-channel function shared by kidney and inner ear.
